title: Japan Airports Test Clothes-Shrinking Machines
paragraphs: Have you ever had a problem closing your suitcase at the end of a trip? Many travelers buy souvenirs and then find that there is no space in their bags. Now, airports in Japan are testing a machine that can make clothes much smaller.

The service is called Pocket Tips. It was made by SJOY, a clothing company in Tokyo, together with a research center at Haneda Airport. The machine is about the size of a bank ATM. It has been tested at four airports in Japan: Haneda and Narita in Tokyo, Kumamoto and Naha.

The machine is easy to use. First, travelers fold their clothes into a special box. Then, they put it into the machine and press a button. In about one minute, the machine presses the clothes until they are up to seven times smaller. Travelers do not need plastic bags, and the machine can even press towels. Later, people can wash their clothes or leave them out for about 15 minutes, and the clothes will go back to their normal shape.

The companies asked 400 people who used the machine about it. About 70% said that in the past, they did not buy souvenirs because they had no space in their luggage. After using the machine, about 89% said they would use it again.
The companies want to start the service fully, possibly in 2027. But they have not said yet how much it will cost.
